newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress OKs single tax for small business.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress OKs single tax for small business.

text.p: Brazil's Congress approved a presidential decree creating a single tax for small and micro-sized companies, an official said.

In a joint session, the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate approved in a symbolic vote the establishment of the new tax, dubbed the "the simple," grouping into one tax eight federal, state and municipal charges now paid by small firms.
Under the new tax, companies earning up to 60,000 reais a year will pay three percent.
The tax will be increased on a sliding scale to a maximum of eight percent, incorporating all three levels of government, for companies earnings up to 120,000 reais a year.

Dep. Augusto Nardes, who represents the small business sector in the lower house, said approximately four million Brazilian firms stood to benefit from the new tax and its simplified bureaucratic requirements.
"It was a great victory for small business," he said.
Dep. Benito Gama, the government's chief whip in the lower house, also welcomed the vote.
"This legislation is of the greatest importance. With the simple we are starting to create the conditions for the creation of more jobs in the country," Gama said.
Earlier Tuesday, the government agreed to reduce the tax rate from between five and 10 percent, which the small business sector said was too high.
